task_summary:
Traveler already has hotel and car reservations and now needs flights built around those fixed dates. Correct resolution: the agent should anchor the flight plan to the existing ground-trip reservations instead of proposing flights that require rebuilding the trip.

Challenge: This tests whether the agent can plan around pre-existing trip state rather than assuming every package starts from scratch.
state_requirements_reasoning: All required state assertions matched the saved state_diff.

task_requirements_details.requirement: Agent must use hotel reservation HR-0100 and car rental CR-0100 as fixed date constraints when proposing flights, including the hotel check-in/check-out and car pickup/dropoff dates.
task_requirements_details.reasoning: The agent explicitly retrieved and referenced hotel reservation HR-0100 (check-in 2026-06-24, check-out 2026-06-27) and car rental CR-0100 (pickup 2026-06-24, dropoff 2026-06-27), then proposed and searched flights on June 24 and June 27 to fit those fixed dates.

task_requirements_details.requirement: Agent must not propose flights that would require changing the already-booked hotel or car dates.
task_requirements_details.reasoning: At no point did the agent propose flights on dates outside June 24–27 or suggest changing the hotel or car dates. All proposed and booked flights were ORD→LAX on 2026-06-24 and LAX→ORD on 2026-06-27, while stating the hotel and car would remain unchanged.

ux_reasoning: The agent handled the core travel challenge well by first retrieving the existing hotel and car, anchoring the flight dates to those reservations, and repeatedly confirming those ground bookings would remain unchanged. It maintained excellent control boundaries: searches and summaries stayed read-only, it previewed price/cabin/preferences clearly, and it correctly did not book when the user said "please go ahead" but had not yet chosen a payment method. User effort was very low because the agent clarified the key budget scope upfront, surfaced the relevant trip dependency about unknown car pickup/drop-off hours, and never required correction or re-steering. Response quality was strong and decision-ready, though slightly short of perfect because several turns repeated the same itinerary summary and the option presentation did not explicitly say whether those were the only matching flights.
